summary: Backend-only tests for iteration 2 features (live piece pricing on products + SIP due reminders) plus full regression. 36/36 pytest cases passed (7 new + 29 existing). Verified: (1) GET /public/products/{id} returns live_price and full pricing{metal_value, making, purity, purity_factor, rate_per_gram, live_price, stale, fetched_at} — aur-rings-0 pricing.making==12500, purity_factor 0.75, metal_value == round(4.2 × gold_rate × 0.75), live_price == round(metal + making) within ±1 rupee, and pricing.rate_per_gram matches /public/rates gold.inr_per_gram. (2) GET /public/products?featured=true — every returned item has a positive live_price and a pricing block whose live_price matches the top-level live_price. (3) 22K product (aur-necklaces-2, 18.4g, making 32000) correctly uses purity_factor 0.916. (4) Cross-tenant NOIR (7% gold margin) vs AURELIA (6%) for the equivalent rings-0 SKU — pricing.rate_per_gram differs; ratio ≈ 1.07/1.06 (±0.001) and NOIR live_price > AURELIA live_price while making is identical (12500). (5) SIP reminder source: after POST /sip/enroll, GET /sip/enrollments shows an installment with status='due' and due_date ≤ now (within 5s clock-skew tolerance); after POST .../pay, that installment becomes 'paid' with paid_at set, the next installment (index 2) becomes 'due' with due_date ~30 days in the future (25 < Δdays < 35), and there are zero installments matching (status=='due' AND due_date ≤ now) — i.e. the frontend reminder rule now yields no nudges. Full regression suite (rates/margins/isolation/bootstrap/cms/categories/products/orders/sip flows) still green.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py:_enrich_product_price — rounds metal_value and making independently then rounds their sum for live_price; math holds but tests allow ±1 rupee tolerance between round(a)+round(b) and round(a+b). Acceptable for display.
server.py:PURITY_FACTORS uses float constants — fine for display-only pricing; if this ever backs invoices, switch to Decimal to avoid drift.

server.py:_enrich_product_price falls back to prod['price'] when rates are unavailable and sets pricing=None. Frontend must handle pricing==null to render 'indicative' vs. 'live'. No breakage observed; feed was live during this run.

server.py:sip_enroll — first installment's due_date == start (now, UTC), so it is instantly 'due'. After pay, the promoted installment's due_date is 30 days after the ORIGINAL start, i.e. still ~30 days ahead of 'now' at test time. Works for the demo; a longer real-world gap between enroll and first pay could produce a promoted due_date that's already <= now again. Not a bug for this iteration but worth a note.
server.py:refresh_spot swallows exceptions and keeps the last-known snapshot; stale flag is exposed. Good resilience for the third-party gold-api.com + frankfurter.dev dependencies.
seed_data_creation: No persistent seed changes. Tests create ephemeral SIP enrollments and orders under TEST_ guest_ids only, isolated from real flows.

Three test files under /app/backend/tests/: test_storefront.py (bootstrap/cms/categories/products/isolation), test_rates_sip_orders.py (live rates + SIP + orders + cross-tenant isolation), test_live_pricing_sip_due.py (NEW: product live_price/pricing block + SIP due-date transition). BASE_URL = EXPO_PUBLIC_BACKEND_URL from /app/frontend/.env. AURELIA host = aurelia.luxejewel.app (gold_pct 6, silver_pct 9); NOIR host = noir.luxejewel.app (gold_pct 7, silver_pct 10). Product IDs are tenant-prefixed: aur-* on AURELIA, noi-* on NOIR — noi-* is only fetchable via the NOIR host.
